text: Valley, this is Medic 12 coming to you with a stroke alert. Seventy-one year old female, husband says last known well was 0915. On exam she's got a left facial droop, left arm drifts, left leg holds up fine, and her eyes are deviated to the right. ETA eighteen.
notes: Destination from the radio address ('Valley ... coming to you'). 'Stroke alert' is not a complaint. Unqualified 'left facial droop' -> facial 2. 'Left leg holds up fine' -> leg 0 (negative, no deficit). Gaze deviation is a positive RACE finding, so it is also a deficit (4b).

text: Crushing substernal chest pain, goes up into his left jaw, started at 0640 while he was shoveling the driveway. Fifty-eight, male. Twelve-lead acquired at 0712, ST elevation in II, III and aVF, transmitting to you now.
notes: ecg.attached = true: the 12-lead is stated as acquired (done) and being transmitted now (present, not a future action). ST-elevation leads have no key.

text: Restrained driver, T-boned at maybe forty miles an hour, heavy intrusion on the passenger side, both front airbags deployed. She's complaining of left hip pain. GCS fifteen.
facts: heavy intrusion on the passenger side
notes: 'She's complaining of' treated like c/o -> medic. complaint.chief is single-valued: chose the stated complaint (left hip pain) over the mechanism (MVC/T-bone). Speed is hedged ('maybe forty') -> not recorded. 'GCS fifteen' is a total, not a stated motor score -> no gcs_motor; no ACVPU word -> no consciousness. 'She' alone gives no sex.

text: Daughter came by at lunch and found her like this. Right-sided weakness, speech is slurred. Daughter says she talked to her on the phone at nine last night and she sounded completely normal.
notes: 'Daughter came by at lunch and found her like this' is the daughter's account (tagged attribution) -> onset_witnessed false, family. 'Talked to her on the phone at nine last night and she sounded completely normal' = normal-at -> LKW; 'nine last night' written as '9 pm' (digits; 'last night' gives pm). 'Weakness'/'slurred' are vague -> deficits only, no RACE. 'At lunch' is a discovery time -> no key.

text: County General, Medic 7, we'll be transporting to you, ETA twelve minutes, stand by for full report.
Known COPD'er, tripoding on the edge of the bed, talking in two-word sentences. Resps thirty-two, sats eighty-four on his home two liters. We've got him on CPAP at ten now.
notes: on_oxygen true both for the home 2 L and for the CPAP now (CPAP counts; 'ten' is pressure). One fact since both states are true. COPD history, tripoding and two-word sentences have no key; no complaint word stated.

text: D-stick was thirty-eight, we pushed twenty-five grams of D10, recheck is one forty-four and he's coming around, answering questions.
notes: Recheck = two facts (4b). D10 was given by EMS -> not a home med. 'Coming around, answering questions' is not an ACVPU word (not stated as alert) -> no consciousness fact.

text: She was fine, I mean she was totally fine when I left for the gym at six thirty, and when I got home at seven fifteen she was on the bathroom floor, she couldn't get up.
speaker: husband
notes: Husband on the mic -> family. 'Totally fine when I left ... at six thirty' = fine-at -> LKW '6:30' (no am/pm spoken, none added). Found on the bathroom floor when he got home -> onset_witnessed false. 7:15 is a discovery time, not onset. No complaint word ('couldn't get up' is not a named complaint and a fall is not stated).

text: Unresponsive on arrival, pinpoint pupils, breathing six a minute. Two of Narcan intranasal, and now he's breathing twelve and cussing at us.
notes: RR before and after naloxone = recheck -> two facts. Narcan given by EMS -> not a home med. 'Cussing at us' is not an ACVPU word -> no second consciousness fact. Pinpoint pupils has no key.

text: It's like an elephant sitting on my chest, it started, I dunno, maybe twenty minutes ago? I took one of my nitroglycerin pills before you guys got here.
speaker: patient
notes: Patient on the mic -> patient. 'Elephant sitting on my chest' stated as the complaint. Onset hedged ('I dunno, maybe twenty minutes ago?') -> no symptom.onset. Nitroglycerin taken before EMS arrived -> home med.

text: RACE: face is symmetric, right arm falls straight to the bed, can't lift it at all, right leg drifts, no gaze deviation, and she's globally aphasic, not getting a single word out.
notes: Arm falls to bed / can't lift -> 2; leg drifts -> 1; globally aphasic -> 2. Negative face/gaze get RACE 0 only.

text: Ground level fall, uh, tripped over the dog and hit her head on the coffee table. Per patient, no loss of consciousness. She's on warfarin for a mechanical valve.
notes: 'Per patient, no loss of consciousness' is a negation with no key. 'She's on warfarin' is a new sentence -> medic, not governed by 'per patient'. Head strike folded into the single complaint.

text: He takes the Humalog with meals and Lantus at bedtime, and he skipped supper tonight 'cause he wasn't feeling good. I found him all sweaty and mumbling around eight thirty.
speaker: wife
notes: Wife on the mic -> family. Humalog -> insulin lispro, Lantus -> insulin glargine. 'I found him all sweaty and mumbling' = found with symptoms -> onset_witnessed false (applied the guide's 'found' rule regardless of the presumed cause). 'Around eight thirty' is a discovery time, not onset. 'Wasn't feeling good' too vague for a complaint; 'mumbling' is not an ACVPU word.

text: RACE of six, screens positive for LVO, requesting you activate the stroke team ahead of our arrival.
notes: RACE total only -> no item scores (4b). LVO screen / stroke-team activation is not a complaint.

text: Sixteen, known asthmatic, hit her ProAir four times in the last hour, no relief. We gave a DuoNeb. Diffuse wheezes, sats ninety-one.
notes: Leading 'Sixteen' read as age. ProAir -> albuterol, used by the patient before EMS -> home med. DuoNeb given by EMS -> excluded. No complaint word stated (asthma history and wheezes are not a named complaint); 'her' gives no sex.

text: Seventy-nine year old female from Maplewood with a Foley. The nurse there says she spiked to one oh three point six and has been lethargic since this morning. Pressure eighty-four over fifty, heart rate one twenty-two.
notes: Nursing-home nurse = facility staff -> family. 103.6 F -> 39.8 C. 'Lethargic' has no ACVPU mapping in the guide -> kept as the complaint (not already captured by a structured key); its onset 'since this morning' is in the same attributed clause. Foley and 'from Maplewood' have no key.

text: pt is on eliquess for a fib per the son last dose this morning left arm and leg are weak no facial droop
notes: 'eliquess' is ASR for Eliquis -> apixaban. Unpunctuated 'per the son' read as governing the preceding med clause (and the last-dose clause, which has no key). 'Weak' is vague -> deficit only, no RACE arm/leg. 'No facial droop' -> facial 0.

text: Gave three twenty-four of aspirin, chewed, and one nitro sublingual. Pressure before the nitro was one fifty-two over ninety, sorry, one thirty-two over ninety.
notes: Aspirin and nitro given by EMS -> not home meds. Correction 152 -> 132; DBP 90 unchanged.

text: I saw the whole thing, the truck turned left right in front of him and he went flying over the handlebars. No helmet. He was knocked out for like a minute.
speaker: bystander
facts: thrown over the handlebars after a truck turned in front of him
notes: Bystander on the mic -> bystander. Mechanism of injury counts as complaint. 'I saw the whole thing' -> onset_witnessed true (the guide's witnessed rule applied literally even though this is trauma; judgment call). 'Knocked out for like a minute' is hedged and has no key.

text: Clearing St. Luke's, back in service.
notes: Clearing a hospital after transport is not a destination.

text: Aide at the nursing home says she was at her baseline for the two a.m. bed check and they found her like this at six. On our arrival she has a left facial droop and she's not moving the left arm at all.
notes: Nursing-home aide -> family. 'At her baseline for the two a.m. bed check' -> LKW '2 am'. 'Found her like this at six' -> onset_witnessed false; six is a discovery time. 'Not moving the left arm at all' = no movement -> arm 2. Exam findings follow 'On our arrival' -> medic.

text: sugar reads four hundred eighty seven kussmaul breathing around thirty fruity breath per mom shes been vomiting since yesterday shes fourteen and on an insulin pump
notes: 'Breathing around thirty' -> RR 30 (an approximate count, not a hedge; not tagged uncertain). Unpunctuated 'per mom' read as governing only 'she's been vomiting since yesterday'; age and insulin pump are medic. Insulin pump -> meds.list ['insulin']. Kussmaul breathing / fruity breath have no key.

text: Per the daughter, cough and fever for three days. Temp's 102.4, resp rate twenty-six, sat eighty-nine percent on room air, and she's confused, which the daughter says is new.
notes: 102.4 F -> 39.1 C. Consciousness C attributed to the medic: 'she's confused' is the medic's own observation; the daughter only adds that it is new.

text: Passed out in the pew during the service, people around her say she was out maybe thirty seconds. Denies chest pain beforehand. Takes Toprol and hydrochlorothiazide. Ninety-two over fifty-eight sitting up.
notes: Bystanders' LOC duration is hedged ('maybe thirty seconds') and has no key. onset_witnessed not labeled: 'people around her say she was out' implies but does not state the collapse was seen. Denied chest pain -> no fact. Toprol -> metoprolol. 'Ninety-two over fifty-eight' is an X-over-Y BP.

text: I wasn't there, but Mrs. Alvarez next door told me she saw Dad getting the mail at ten and he waved and talked to her, totally normal. Then he called me at eleven thirty and his words were all slurred.
speaker: daughter
notes: Nested attribution: the neighbor saw him normal at ten -> LKW, bystander (4b); no am/pm spoken -> '10'. Slurred words were heard by the daughter herself on the phone -> family. 11:30 is when symptoms were noticed, not their onset -> no symptom.onset.

text: st elevation mi alert inferior leads pt is 64 yo female diaphoretic and pale bp 88/50 hr 44 were 11 minutes out to st marys cath lab
notes: 'STEMI alert' treated like 'stroke alert' -> not a complaint. ST elevation in the inferior leads implies a 12-lead, but none is mentioned as done or attached -> no ecg facts. Diaphoretic/pale have no key. 'st marys cath lab' -> destination 'St. Mary's'.

text: He says he was, uh, jumped by two guys outside the bar, got kicked in the ribs a bunch. Denies hitting his head. Breathing's twenty-four and shallow, sats ninety-three.
notes: 'He says he was jumped ... kicked in the ribs' -> mechanism (assault) as complaint, patient. Denied head strike -> no fact.

text: Stroke alert, stroke alert. LKW fourteen hundred, correction, thirteen hundred per the wife. Right facial droop, mild, and right arm drift.
notes: Correction 1400 -> 1300; 'per the wife' governs the LKW only. 'Right facial droop, mild' -> facial 1.

text: Hey, can somebody grab the stair chair out of the rig, and the extra O2 bottle?
Staff at Oak Hill says she's more confused than her baseline since yesterday morning. Dementia at baseline, normally A and O times one. Temp ninety-nine point one.
notes: Facility staff -> family. 'More confused than her baseline' -> C, not a complaint (v1_039). Baseline 'A and O times one' describes baseline, not current state -> no A. 99.1 F -> 37.3 C. Dementia history has no key.

text: Roommate thinks he went to bed normal, maybe around midnight, but honestly he's not sure, he got home late himself. Patient woke up with the whole left side not working.
notes: Roommate's LKW is hedged ('thinks', 'maybe', 'not sure') -> no LKW. 'Patient woke up with ...' is stated by the medic without attribution -> onset_witnessed false, medic. Vague deficit -> no RACE.

text: Known peanut allergy, ate a cookie at a birthday party, throat feels tight and she's covered in hives. Used her own EpiPen at 1935 before we got here, we just gave a second epi IM.
notes: Own EpiPen used before EMS arrived -> home med (epinephrine, 4b); the second epi given by EMS is an intervention. 1935 is a medication time, no key.

text: He's on Crestor and lisinopril, and he has the nitro spray but he didn't use it. No blood thinners, the cardiologist took him off the Eliquis last year.
speaker: wife
notes: Wife on the mic -> family. Crestor -> rosuvastatin. Nitro spray included: it is his own prescribed PRN medication even though he did not use it this time (judgment call). Eliquis was stopped last year -> not in the list. 'No blood thinners' -> anticoagulant 'none'.

text: Fell, uh, roughly twelve feet off a ladder cleaning gutters, landed flat on his back on the driveway. Fifty-two, male, says he can't feel his feet.
notes: Fall height is hedged ('roughly twelve feet') but the fall itself is stated. 'Says he can't feel his feet' -> patient; labeled as a deficit because it is a stated neurological deficit and stroke.deficits is the only key for it (judgment call on a trauma call).

text: Okay so, uh, face is symmetric, left arm drifts, left leg's fine, eyes are parked to the right, and she doesn't recognize her left arm as her own, but she does know she's weak.
notes: 'Eyes parked to the right' = gaze deviation -> 1. Doesn't recognize the arm but does recognize the weakness -> agnosia 1.

text: Orthostatics: heart rate seventy-four lying, one-oh-eight standing, uh, correction, one-eighteen standing.
notes: Orthostatic lying and standing values are two readings -> two facts (like a recheck); the standing value is corrected 108 -> 118, so 108 is dropped.

text: BGL fifty-three, sorry, thirty-five, I flipped the digits. She's only responding to voice.
notes: Correction 53 -> 35.

text: wife says hes been sleeping in the recliner cause he cant lay flat and he takes lasics and coreg bp 196/104 sats 86 crackles up to the shoulders
notes: Run-on ASR: 'and he takes lasics and coreg' is conjoined to the wife's statement -> family. 'lasics' = Lasix -> furosemide; Coreg -> carvedilol. Orthopnea ('can't lay flat') is the stated complaint. Vitals and crackles follow as the medic's findings; crackles have no key.

text: Wife watched it happen at quarter past seven, he was reading the paper and just stopped talking mid-sentence. Now he can't get any words out and the right side's weak.
notes: 'Wife watched it happen' is the wife's account (tagged attribution) -> family. Clock time of a witnessed onset -> symptom.onset, not LKW; 'quarter past seven' -> '7:15'. 'Now he can't get any words out' = can't speak -> aphasia 2 (medic). 'Right side's weak' is vague -> no arm/leg RACE.

text: Change of plans, we're diverting to Kaiser Santa Clara, Valley's on CT divert. New ETA twenty-two.
notes: Valley is on divert, not the destination.

text: Thirty-one year old guy, sharp chest pain that's worse lying flat and better leaning forward, had the flu last week. Temp one hundred point nine, heart rate one oh six, ninety-eight percent on room air.
notes: 'Guy' is a sex descriptor noun (like 'lady'), not a pronoun -> M. 100.9 F -> 38.3 C. 'Ninety-eight percent on room air' -> SpO2 98 even without the word 'sats'. Recent flu is history, no key.

text: She fell off the monkey bars, maybe ten minutes ago, and her arm looks bent the wrong way. She's seven. She's allergic to amoxicillin, it gives her a rash.
speaker: mom
notes: Mom on the mic -> family. Onset hedged ('maybe ten minutes ago') -> no symptom.onset. Arm deformity folded into the single complaint. Reaction type (rash) is not part of the allergen value.

text: medic 4 to mercy stroke alert 80 year old mail last known well 3:45 pm per caregiver right face droop right arm and leg flaccid glucose 132 eta 9
notes: 'mail' is the ASR homophone of 'male' -> M. Caregiver -> family, governs the LKW only. Unqualified 'right face droop' -> 2; flaccid -> 2.

text: He was shaking all over for like two minutes, and his temp was 103.1 when I checked it at home. He's four. He's never had a seizure before, ever.
speaker: mom
notes: Mom on the mic -> family, including the home temperature she measured. 103.1 F -> 39.5 C. 'Like two minutes' is the event's duration, not an onset time. 'Never had a seizure' is history, no key.

text: Family thinks he might be diabetic, maybe on some kind of pill for it, but nobody's really sure.
notes: Entirely hedged -> no facts.

text: He's three. The barky cough started last night around eleven, and he's never had anything like this. No allergies.
speaker: dad
notes: Dad on the mic -> family. 'Last night around eleven' -> '11 pm' (approximator dropped, 'last night' gives pm; not a hedge and not tagged uncertain). 'No allergies' -> [].

text: She's a little slurred, and she tells me her left hand's felt clumsy since, she thinks, maybe an hour ago, she's not sure exactly.
notes: 'A little slurred' is the medic's observation; the clumsy hand is patient-reported -> two deficit facts split by role. Onset hedged ('she thinks, maybe ... not sure') -> no symptom.onset. Vague deficits -> no RACE.

text: Per the charge nurse at Sunrise, she was found on the floor next to her bed at 0400, unwitnessed. Left leg's shortened and externally rotated. POLST on file says DNR.
notes: Charge nurse = facility staff -> family. 0400 is when she was found -> neither LKW nor onset. Shortened, externally rotated leg is an exam finding with no key; no complaint word stated ('fall' is implied, not said). 'POLST on file says DNR' is a new sentence the medic reads from the document -> medic.

text: Denies shortness of breath, denies nausea, pain doesn't radiate, no cardiac history.
notes: All negations of symptoms/history -> no facts.

text: Scene's got an empty bottle of Seroquel and a half-empty Xanax bottle on the nightstand. Boyfriend thinks she took maybe twenty of them, but he honestly doesn't know.
facts: empty bottle of Seroquel on the nightstand
half-empty Xanax bottle on the nightstand
notes: Bottles at the scene are scene observations; they are not stated as her medications -> no meds.list. Boyfriend's pill count is hedged -> no fact.

text: Mom takes Coumadin, the Lipitor, and something for her thyroid, I think it's Synthroid? She's allergic to penicillin.
speaker: son
notes: Son on the mic -> family. Coumadin -> warfarin, Lipitor -> atorvastatin. Synthroid is hedged ('I think it's Synthroid?') -> excluded.

text: dispatch medic 3 show us on scene one patient will advise
Blood sugar's, um, sixty-one. She's on Glucophage and Jardiance, and her son says she hasn't eaten since Tuesday.
notes: Glucophage -> metformin, Jardiance -> empagliflozin. Son's 'hasn't eaten since Tuesday' has no key (not a complaint or a symptom onset).

text: unit 22 to regional trauma we have a 19 year old female unrestrained rollover ejected bp 86 over 40 heart rate 130 gcs 9 motor 5 eta 6 minutes
notes: Mechanism of injury -> complaint. GCS total 9 has no key; motor 5 stated -> gcs_motor 5.

text: She won't tolerate anything on her face. Let's see if she'll let us try a nasal cannula in a minute.
notes: Nasal cannula is a future action -> no on_oxygen.

text: Repeat stroke exam at 1420: no droop, both arms hold without drift, no leg drift either, gaze midline, following commands and naming objects fine.
notes: All negative -> RACE 0s only, no deficits. Exam time 1420 has no key.

text: pt states the chest pain comes and goes since around four takes lipiter and metoprolol and a baby aspirin every day
notes: 'lipiter' = Lipitor -> atorvastatin. 'Since around four' -> 'since 4' (approximator dropped). The meds clause 'takes ...' starts a new subjectless medic-shorthand sentence (same pattern as v2_024) -> medic, not governed by 'pt states'. Aspirin is an antiplatelet -> no anticoagulant.

text: Forty-three, no, sorry, thirty-four year old female, right lower quadrant pain since last night, allergic to codeine and latex.
notes: Correction 43 -> 34.

text: Single stab wound to the left flank. Bystander says the guy who did it might've had a second knife, not sure if he got stabbed more than once. That's the only wound I can find.
facts: stab wound to the left flank
notes: Bystander's statement is hedged ('might've', 'not sure') -> no fact.

text: History of A-fib, and husband says she's on Pradaxa, no, sorry, he's correcting himself, it's Xarelto.
notes: Correction Pradaxa -> Xarelto: only rivaroxaban. A-fib history has no key.

text: were gonna head to good sam eta is like eight minutes
notes: 'Like eight minutes' treated as a colloquial approximation, not a hedge (not tagged uncertain).

text: Eyes open to pain, incomprehensible sounds, localizes, so GCS two, two, five, nine total. Sugar's ninety-eight.
notes: Motor 5 stated ('localizes', 'two, two, five'). No ACVPU label: 'eyes open to pain' is a GCS eye component; mapping it to P would be a derivation, not a stated ACVPU level. GCS total 9 has no key.

text: Sats eighty-nine, I mean ninety-eight, the probe was on her nail polish, now reading ninety-eight on room air. Resps eighteen, unlabored.
notes: Correction 89 -> 98; 'now reading ninety-eight' repeats the same corrected value -> one fact.

text: Patient states the room's been spinning and she can't walk a straight line for the past two hours. Denies weakness or numbness. Speech sounds normal to me.
notes: 'Patient states' governs the vertigo, gait and onset -> patient. Gait difficulty is a stated deficit (patient-reported). 'Speech sounds normal to me' is a neuro observation -> aphasia/agnosia 0 per the guide's 'normal speech'. Denied weakness/numbness -> no facts.

text: Let's get her on the monitor, and I'll do a twelve-lead once we're in the truck.
notes: Monitor and 12-lead are future actions.

text: Memorial, Medic 9, we're twelve out, check that, fifteen minutes out, traffic's backed up on the bridge. Pressure's holding at one oh eight over seventy.
notes: Correction 'check that' 12 -> 15.

text: He's calm, cooperative, sitting on the curb with PD, says he just wants to go home.
notes: 'Calm, cooperative' is not an ACVPU word; wanting to go home has no key.

text: Collapsed at the checkout line about twenty minutes ago per the store manager, witnessed. Gaze is deviated left, right arm's flaccid, and he's grunting, no real words.
notes: Store manager = bystander; 'per the store manager, witnessed' governs the collapse, its time and witnessed. 'About twenty minutes ago' -> '20 minutes ago'. 'Grunting, no real words' = severe aphasia -> 2.

text: pts now a and o times 4 sugar 112 after the oral glucose wants to refuse transport
notes: 'a and o times 4' -> A. Oral glucose is a treatment, not a home med. Refusal has no key.

text: Okay vitals, BP is, um, one-ten over seventy, hang on, cuff slipped, one-forty over eighty-six. Heart rate ninety-two, resps twenty.
notes: 'Hang on, cuff slipped' invalidates the first reading -> correction (only 140/86), not a recheck.

text: On my count. One, two, three.
Found at the bottom of the basement stairs, probably fourteen steps, blood on the landing. His wife heard a thump and came running.
facts: found at the bottom of the basement stairs
notes: 'Found at the bottom of the basement stairs' (medic, no attribution) -> onset_witnessed false; the wife only heard a thump, she did not see it. Step count is hedged ('probably'). No complaint: a fall is implied but not stated.

text: She uses the Spiriva every morning and the rescue inhaler, the albuterol, she's used it like six times today. She quit smoking back in 2019.
speaker: husband
notes: Husband on the mic -> family. Spiriva -> tiotropium. Smoking history has no key.

text: so the wife says he was normal last night went to bed at ten thirty and woke up at 6 with his right side weak and he cant talk right
notes: The whole run-on is the wife's account -> family. 'Normal last night, went to bed at ten thirty' -> LKW '10:30 pm' ('last night' gives pm). Woke up with symptoms -> false; 'woke up at 6' is discovery, not onset. Vague deficits -> no RACE.

text: Temp thirty-eight point nine tympanic, heart rate one-ten, resps twenty-four, and she's only responding to voice. Daughter says she's been coughing up green stuff for about four days.
notes: Temperature already Celsius (tympanic). 'For about four days' -> 'for 4 days' (approximator dropped).

text: Her husband says she's been nauseated and short of breath since lunch. She tells me the worst part is a pain between her shoulder blades. Seventy-six, diabetic, takes Lantus at night.
notes: Two complaint sources; complaint.chief is single-valued, so chose the patient's own 'worst part' (pain between the shoulder blades) over the husband's nausea/SOB. The only stated onset ('since lunch') belongs to the husband's clause -> family. 'Diabetic' is history, no key. Lantus -> insulin glargine.

text: Mild left facial droop, left arm drifts down in about five seconds, left leg can't come off the bed, eyes midline. BP two oh four over one twelve, pulse sixty-eight and irregular.
facts: left leg can't come off the bed
notes: Arm drifts down in about 5 s (< 10 s) -> 1. Leg can't come off the bed -> 2. Irregular pulse has no key.

text: Neighbor found him down in the backyard, probably out there all night. Core temp ninety-three point two, and he only responds to pain.
notes: Neighbor found him down -> onset_witnessed false, bystander. 'Probably out there all night' is hedged -> no fact. 93.2 F -> 34.0 C.

text: Security found him slumped over the wheel in the parking garage. Looks to be in his sixties, no ID on him. He's confused, keeps asking where he is. Sugar twenty-nine.
notes: Security guard = bystander (not facility caregiver staff). Found slumped over the wheel -> onset_witnessed false. Age estimate ('looks to be in his sixties') is not a stated age -> no patient.age. 'No ID on him' kept as the medic's scene observation.

text: We were headed to Regional, scratch that, family wants her at Mercy since that's where her doctors are, so Mercy it is.
notes: Regional retracted ('scratch that'). The destination decision is stated by the medic ('so Mercy it is') -> medic, even though the family requested it.

text: Grandma hasn't been right since breakfast. She keeps dropping stuff with her left hand and her mouth looks crooked. She takes Plavix and the metoprolol.
speaker: granddaughter
facts: dropping things with her left hand
notes: Granddaughter on the mic -> family. 'Hasn't been right since breakfast' = onset, not LKW. Lay 'mouth looks crooked' is not an exam finding -> deficit only, no RACE facial. Plavix -> clopidogrel (antiplatelet) -> no anticoagulant.

text: Neighbor says he hit him with Narcan before we got here. Possible overdose, we don't know on what. Resps are ten, sats eighty-eight.
notes: Naloxone given by the neighbor is a bystander intervention, not a home medication -> not in meds.list. 'Possible overdose, we don't know on what' is hedged -> no complaint.

text: Pelvis is unstable. BP ninety-eight over sixty, I misread that, seventy-eight over sixty. Pulse one twenty-eight and thready.
notes: Correction 98 -> 78 SBP. Unstable pelvis is an exam finding with no key.

text: Sudden onset SOB about an hour ago, just flew back from Tokyo. She's on birth control and denies any blood thinners. HR one-eighteen, sats ninety-two on four liters by cannula.
notes: 'About an hour ago' -> '1 hour ago'. 'Birth control' kept as said (no drug name given to map to a generic). 'Denies any blood thinners' -> 'none', and 'denies' makes it patient; 'She's on birth control' has no attribution verb -> medic. Travel history has no key.

text: Pain's an eight out of ten. Gave fifty mics of fentanyl IV at 1510, and I'll repeat the twelve-lead en route.
notes: Fentanyl given by EMS. 'I'll repeat the twelve-lead' is a future action; it presupposes an earlier 12-lead but none is stated as done -> no ecg facts. Pain score has no key; unlocated 'pain' not labeled as a complaint.

text: black tarry stools for 2 days on zarelto for afib hr 124 bp 90/56 pale and weak
notes: 'zarelto' is ASR for Xarelto -> rivaroxaban. Generalized 'weak' is not a focal deficit.

text: Group home staff say she woke up like this, unwitnessed, and last known well was their bed check at twenty-two hundred. Sats ninety-seven room air, sugar one eighteen.
notes: Group-home staff = facility caregivers -> family.

text: i just take the zocor and the blood pressure one norvasc no allergies that i know of
speaker: patient
notes: Patient on the mic. Zocor -> simvastatin, Norvasc -> amlodipine. 'No allergies that I know of' is the standard NKA phrasing, not a hedge (tagged negation, not uncertain) -> [].

text: His chest started hurting at nine, no wait, eight thirty, he called me right after. He's allergic to sulfa and, um, maybe morphine? I'm not sure about the morphine.
speaker: daughter
notes: Daughter on the mic -> family. Correction nine -> eight thirty. Morphine allergy hedged -> excluded.

text: Um, ED, Medic 15, uh, we're, we're about five minutes out with the, uh, the chest pain patient I called in earlier.
notes: 'About five minutes out' -> 5. 'The chest pain patient' states the complaint. 'ED' is not a hospital name -> no destination.

text: Um, she's got a, a left, no, a right-sided facial droop, pretty subtle actually, and the right arm is, uh, drifting.
notes: Self-correction left -> right. 'Pretty subtle' = mild -> facial 1.

text: Roofer, out in the sun all day, core temp one oh four point two, sorry, one oh five point two. He's confused and he's stopped sweating.
notes: Correction 104.2 -> 105.2 F -> 40.7 C. Sun exposure and anhidrosis have no key; no complaint word stated.

text: Choking on steak at the restaurant, a bystander did the Heimlich and it came out before we arrived. She's talking fine now, sats ninety-nine, lungs clear.
notes: Bystander's Heimlich is an intervention. 'Talking fine now' refers to the airway, not a language exam -> no RACE aphasia item.

text: Ped struck at low speed, thrown onto the hood, starred windshield. Sats ninety on room air, now ninety-six on a non-rebreather.
notes: Two readings (room air, then non-rebreather) -> two SpO2 facts and both oxygen states, as with a recheck.

text: He's A and O times four, pale, cool and clammy. Rate's in the forties, forty-two on the monitor, pressure ninety-four over sixty. Pads are on.
notes: 'Rate's in the forties' refined to 42 in the same breath -> one HR fact. 'Pads are on' = defib/pacing pads, not a 12-lead -> no ecg facts.

text: She's on hospice, she has a DNR, the paper's on the fridge. We just want her comfortable. Her breathing changed about an hour ago.
speaker: son
notes: Son on the mic -> family. Hospice has no key. The paper's location is the son's report, not a medic scene observation.

text: Complete left facial paralysis, left arm and leg are flaccid, head and eyes turned to the right. She insists nothing's wrong with her, though she does know that's her arm.
facts: head and eyes turned to the right
notes: Insists nothing is wrong (doesn't recognize the deficit) but knows it's her arm -> agnosia 1.

text: Two-car MVC, restrained driver, seatbelt mark across the lower abdomen, c/o belly pain. His wife was the passenger, second unit has her.
notes: c/o -> medic (4b). Seatbelt mark is an exam finding; 'his' is a pronoun -> no sex. The wife is a second patient, not a source.

text: Pulling into the bay now.
NKDA. Takes Eliquis twice a day for a clot in his leg, last dose last night. Full code per his wife.
notes: NKDA -> []. Eliquis -> apixaban. 'Per his wife' governs only the code status.
